summary: Washington DNR lookout built 1965 on Monumental Mountain, Stevens County; removed 1996; top 10 feet rebuilt on Rod Fosback's private land; NHLR-registered 1999.

facts.design: Flat-top 14-by-14-foot DNR cab with catwalk on a 10-foot wood tower (NHLR); the FFLOS record describes the original as a 40-foot DNR timber tower
facts.status_note: Only the top 10 feet of the original DNR tower survive, rebuilt on private land after the 1996 removal

staffing.status: Not staffed; the Register says the Fosback family would staff it as a volunteer service if fire conditions warrant

access.note: On private land overlooking the Little Pend Oreille River; no visiting arrangement is described

events.note: 60-foot pole tower with cabin built on Monumental Mountain (FFLOS); a 1945 road and observation cabin are reported by the Forest Lookouts page
Dan Reeder of Rice employed as lookout at the summit cabin
Washington DNR built a 40-foot timber tower with a live-in cab, replacing the 1945 tower. The Forest Lookouts page gives 1964-66
FFLOS says last staffed in 1980; the Register says staffed until the mid 1980s
Tower removed from the summit to make room for another radio tower
Sold to FFLA member Rod Fosback, who moved it to his own woodland (Register)
firelookout.com says Fosback rescued the tower and placed it on his hillside property in 1998
Registered November 18, 1999 as US 330, WA 36; nominated by Ray Kresek, Washington Registrar

corrections.current: None relocated (Moved from Monumental Mountain to Fosback.)
corrections.proposed: Removed from Monumental Mountain in 1996 and sold to Rod Fosback; placed on his hillside property in 1998
corrections.why: The 'None relocated' label contradicts the note that the tower was moved, and the record omits the 1996 removal and the 1965 build.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS describes a 40-foot DNR timber tower of 1965, of which the top 10 feet were rebuilt; the Register and firelookout.com describe the surviving 10-foot tower with the cab. Both are recorded; the story reads them as the original and the surviving section.
FFLOS gives 1980 as the last staffed year; the Register says staffed until the mid 1980s. Both are kept.

The Register and the Forest Lookouts page give 1996 for the sale and move; firelookout.com says the tower was placed on Fosback's property in 1998. The sources do not explain the two years; both are kept.

notes_for_editor: Do not conflate with the separate Monumental Mountain Lookout Site on the Colville National Forest (US 1515, WA 415, Pend Oreille County, 5,700 ft), a 1926 detection site with a pole tower replaced in 1939 and removed in 1958; that record is separate and the record's source_pages link to it. The Stevens County site (US 1514, WA 414) is the one this record describes, with the 1945 pole tower and the 1965 DNR tower. The Register says the tower is ready for volunteer staffing if needed; no staffing is recorded after the early-to-mid 1980s. Visiting is not described, and the site is private land, so the story advises asking the owners.
